title: Calling a parent mama, dada, or another special name is a 1-year CDC item
summary: By the first birthday, CDC says most babies use mama, dada, or another special name for a parent.
body: The 1-year CDC sheet treats mama, dada, or some other special name as address aimed at a parent. That is a person-name, not a chain of one syllable produced for its sound. Waving bye-bye sits on the same sheet and is a hand gesture, so it is outside this entry. A brief pause when someone says no is also a different entry. The naming entry is a United States group mark for the first birthday. A baby who is not there yet has not received a diagnosis from the line.
